outline.description: This chapter introduces the parties, the Cameo platform context, the factual circumstances giving rise to the dispute, the procedural history in the District Court, and the standard of review applied by the Second Circuit on appeal.
subtopics: The parties: George Santos, Jimmy Kimmel, ABC, and Disney
The Cameo platform and personalized video request mechanism
The factual dispute: Kimmel's use of fictitious names and the 'Will Santos Say It?' segments
District Court proceedings and dismissal under Rule 12(b)(6)
Standard of review: de novo review of a motion to dismiss
Materials the court may consider on a 12(b)(6) motion

outline.chapter_title: Copyright Infringement and the Fair Use Doctrine
outline.description: This chapter explains the framework for copyright infringement claims, introduces fair use as an affirmative defense under Section 107 of the Copyright Act, outlines the four statutory factors, and discusses when fair use can be resolved at the pleading stage.
subtopics: Elements of a copyright infringement claim
Fair use as an affirmative defense to copyright infringement
Section 107 and the four statutory fair use factors
Judicial notice of copyright registrations
Fair use resolution at the pleading stage

outline.chapter_title: Application of Fair Use Factors in Santos v. Kimmel
outline.description: This chapter provides a detailed analysis of how the Second Circuit applied each of the four fair use factors to Santos's claims, including the transformative use analysis, the rejection of Santos's bad faith argument, and the market harm analysis.
subtopics: Purpose and character of use: transformative use and commentary
The reasonable observer standard versus subjective intent
Nature of the copyrighted work and publication timing
Amount and substantiality of the portion used
Effect on potential market: market harm versus market criticism
Bad faith argument and its rejection under Harper & Row

outline.description: This chapter examines Santos's breach of contract and implied contract claims, including the third-party beneficiary doctrine under Illinois law, the requirements for pleading an implied contract under New York law, and the court's alternative discussion of Copyright Act preemption.
subtopics: Direct breach of contract claim under the Cameo Terms of Service
Third-party beneficiary doctrine and Illinois law's strong presumption against third-party enforcement
Express declaration requirement for third-party beneficiary status
Implied contract claim under New York law
Meeting of the minds and essential terms requirements
Copyright Act preemption as an alternative ground for dismissal

outline.description: This chapter analyzes Santos's fraudulent inducement claim, explaining the elements under New York law, the critical out-of-pocket loss requirement, and why Santos's allegations failed to state a claim for relief.
subtopics: Elements of fraudulent inducement under New York law
The out-of-pocket loss requirement
Application to Santos's allegations of Kimmel's deception
The absence of pleaded actual damages
